Here are two classic, citable sources (plus an optional textbook) you can drop in a footnote—no links, just named references:

1) Barry W. Boehm, Software Engineering Economics. Prentice‑Hall, 1981.  
   - Classic presentation of the cost‑of‑change/defect‑fix escalation: defects become far more expensive to fix the later they are discovered.

2) Capers Jones, Applied Software Measurement: Assuring Productivity and Quality. McGraw‑Hill, 1991.  
   - Empirical measurements and discussion showing defect removal costs rise substantially in later phases and in production.

Optional textbook (if you want a general textbook citation):  
- Ian Sommerville, Software Engineering (Pearson).  
  - Standard textbook treatment of the cost of change and defect removal across development phases.

If you want exact page numbers or a specific edition for any of these for a formal citation, tell me which one and I can look up the precise edition/pages.
